description: The national flower of both Argentina and Uruguay. A spreading tree whose brilliant red flowers carry the whole spring and summer.
nativeStatus: Native to the Río de la Plata region
ecology: Associated with wetlands, river margins and low ground. A nitrogen-fixing legume, so it improves the soil for everything planted around it.
wildlifeNotes: A hummingbird magnet in spring and summer. The picaflor común (Chlorostilbon lucidus) depends heavily on it, and large native bees work the same flowers.
soil: Tolerates moist and seasonally wet soils
size: Altura / height: 6-12 m. Porte: árbol mediano, ancho y abierto.
medicinalUses: In rioplatense medicine the bark tea is an astringent, antiseptic and sedative. Indigenous peoples used the bark on wounds and for toothache. The alkaloids erythraline and erysodine carry the sedative and anxiolytic action.
sources: Sendero de flora nativa, Jardín Botánico de Buenos Aires: https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/jardinbotanico/senderofloranativa
notes: Ya tenemos ceibo en el sanctuario. / Already in the sanctuary.
